They ensure that all parachutes are packed properly and serviceable for airborne operations. Rigging personnel also train soldiers on parachute procedures and occasionally participate in jumps to verify equipment performance. Their work is critical for the safety of airborne troops and cargo drops.What are the key skills and qualifications needed to thrive in the 92R Parachute Rigger position, and why are they important?To excel as a 92R Parachute Rigger, you need attention to detail, manual dexterity, physical stamina, and basic mechanical aptitude, usually acquired through Army training and certification. Familiarity with technical sewing machines, inspection tools, and strict adherence to documented procedures and safety protocols is required. Exceptional teamwork, problem-solving abilities, and a strong sense of responsibility distinguish outstanding riggers. These competencies are critical as riggers ensure parachutes function flawlessly, directly impacting the safety of airborne personnel and mission success.What does a typical workday look like for a 92R Parachute Rigger in the Army?As a 92R Parachute Rigger, your day often starts with inspecting and preparing parachutes and related equipment for upcoming airborne operations. Duties also include performing repairs, maintaining packing areas, conducting rigorous safety checks, and documenting all maintenance activities. Riggers commonly work as part of tight-knit teams, collaborating closely with jumpmasters and other logistics personnel. While the work can be physically demanding and requires strict attention to detail, it is highly rewarding knowing your efforts directly contribute to the safety and effectiveness of airborne missions.How much does a 92R make in the army?A 92R Parachute Rigger in the U.S. Army typically earns a salary based on rank and years of service, with base pay ranging from approximately $25,000 to over $50,000 annually. Additional allowances, bonuses, and benefits can increase total compensation, and the role requires specialized skills in packing and maintaining parachutes and safety equipment.How much money do parachute riggers make?Parachute riggers typically earn between $40,000 and $70,000 annually, depending on experience, certifications, and the employer. Military parachute riggers may have different pay scales, often aligned with military pay grades, and additional benefits may apply.
